'''Silvash gombotz''' (Hungarian spelling: Szilvás gombóc) is a traditional [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] recipe for plum dumplings from Hungary. During the freezing cold winters, warm filling desserts like these are very popular.

==Ingredients==

*2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] peeled [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Egg|egg]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*3 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
*⅔ pound [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|plain flour]]
*Fresh [[Cookbook:Plum|plums]], plum [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]] or plum [[Cookbook:Compote|compote]]

==Procedure==
#Cook potatoes until very soft (at least an hour). Peel and [[Cookbook:Mashing|mash]] with a fork.
#Add the egg to the mixture, along with the little salt and oil. Mix well.
#Gradually mix in the flour to make a smooth [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. You may need a little more or less than the listed quantity.
#[[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] the potato dough, then [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|roll it out]] into a thin sheet (about 5 mm thick), and cut into squares.
#Put half a plum or 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] of plum jam on each square. Wrap the dough around the filling and seal the edges.
#Cook in boiling water for 10–15 minutes until the dumplings are floating and cooked through.
#Serve with [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|bread crumbs]] fried in [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]].

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* When filled with [[Cookbook:Apricot|apricot]], the dumplings are called "barackos gombóc" or "Baratzkosh Gombotz".
